attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the three-node AlmaLinux 9 cluster: node1 initialized as primary, node2 and node3 cloned via pg_basebackup as async standbys (firewalld opened for the postgresql service; replication role/credentials generated on-node and rotated after an accidental partial exposure in a debug echo). Demonstrated failover by writing a final transaction, stopping PostgreSQL on node1 (simulated primary loss), confirming zero data loss on both standbys, promoting node2 with pg_ctl promote, repointing node3 to follow node2, and rejoining node1 as a fresh standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 primary, node1 and node3 standbys, all data consistent. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and health on all three nodes, rebooted them one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, and proved a changed boot_id plus recovered PostgreSQL role/replication/data (row count 7) after each restart, always keeping at least one other node up as an independent recovery path.
